mainTopic: פאה and חשד, rules and priorities for נר חנוכה, rewards for lighting candles and honoring Torah scholars, and why one may not light with שמן שריפה.
overview: This amud opens partway through a ברייתא that the גמרא quoted to prove that חז"ל worry about חשד (suspicion). The ברייתא lists four reasons why פאה must be left at the end of the field, and רבא explains that the fourth reason is about cheaters. The גמרא then returns to נר חנוכה and rules on lamps with several wicks: covered, they count for several people, but uncovered they are a bonfire and count for no one. רבא sets an order of priority for a poor person: נר ביתו comes first, and נר חנוכה beats קידוש היום because of פרסומי ניסא. Next come אגדות. רב הונא lists rewards for being careful with מצוות, and stories show that homes with many lights produced great תלמידי חכמים. רב יוסף and an elder teach that שבת candles should be lit neither too early nor too late, and רבא lists rewards for loving, honoring and fearing Torah scholars. Last, the גמרא returns to the משנה's שמן שריפה, impure תרומה oil. רבה and רב חסדא give two different reasons why one may not light with it.

steps.title: Second reason for פאה at the field's end: keeping the poor from wasting time
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues its list. פאה goes at the end of the field so that poor people are not stuck waiting and watching for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And because of wasting the poor people's time: so that poor people will not sit and keep watch, thinking, 'Now the owner is going to leave פאה.'
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining a ברייתא partway through. It lists why פאה must be left at the end of a field, and here it gives the reason of ביטול עניים, wasting the time of the poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner could leave פאה anywhere, the poor would have to hang around all day in case he suddenly left it. A fixed spot at the end frees them to work elsewhere until harvest is done. The גמרא quoted this ברייתא (from the previous עמוד) mainly for the next reason, חשד.

keyTerms.meaning: The corner of the field left for the poor

steps.confusionAlert: We are suddenly talking about פאה in a סוגיא about נר חנוכה. The גמרא brought this ברייתא to prove that חשד (what onlookers will think) is a real halachic concern. That concern is why a courtyard with two entrances needs two נרות חנוכה.

phrases.english: And because of wasting the time of the poor —
phrases.notes: The second of four reasons in the ברייתא (the first, גזל עניים, was on the previous עמוד).

phrases.english: so that poor people will not be sitting and watching,
thinking, 'Now the owner is leaving פאה.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא begun on the previous עמוד, quoted to show that חשד matters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פאה is left at the end of the field so the poor do not waste their time waiting for it.

steps.title: Third reason: avoiding suspicion
steps.stepSummary: פאה goes at the end of the field so passersby will not suspect the owner of skipping פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And because of suspicion: so that people passing back and forth will not say, 'May a curse come on the man who did not leave פאה in his field.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its third reason, חשד. This is the reason the גמרא actually needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If פאה were left in the middle, the poor would take it quickly, and the owner would go on harvesting the rest. Later passersby would see a fully harvested field and assume he never left פאה. This shows חז"ל make rules just to stop people from wrongly suspecting someone, which supports the חשד rule for נר חנוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Suspicion: what onlookers will wrongly think
Passersby, people going back and forth

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the proof the גמרא was looking for. Concern for חשד is a real halachic factor, which is why a courtyard with two entrances needs two נרות חנוכה.

phrases.english: And because of suspicion —
so that passersby will not say:
May a curse come upon the person
who did not leave פאה in his field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same ברייתא list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פאה is left at the end of the field to avoid passersby suspecting the owner.

steps.title: Fourth reason: the verse 'do not finish off your field'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's last reason is the פסוק of בל תכלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And because of 'You shall not finish off [the corner of your field].'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its list with a fourth reason, the פסוק בל תכלה. This sets up the גמרא's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording of the פסוק (ויקרא כג) is 'לא תכלה פאת שדך,' which suggests that פאה belongs at the very end, the 'finishing' part of the field. The reason is listed separately from the first three.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Do not finish off': the prohibition against harvesting the entire field

phrases.english: And because of 'You shall not finish off.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final item of the ברייתא list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fourth reason for פאה at the end is the פסוק of בל תכלה.

steps.title: Aren't all the reasons really 'do not finish off'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why בל תכלה is a separate reason when every reason is about not harvesting the whole field.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are all of them not because of 'You shall not finish off'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the fourth reason, saying it does not add anything new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every reason in the list explains why the owner must leave the end of the field unharvested, which is exactly what בל תכלה says. So listing it as its own fourth reason seems redundant.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is it then…?' A challenging question formula

phrases.english: Are all of them not
because of 'You shall not finish off'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ כּוּלְּהוּ לָאו מִשּׁוּם ״בַּל תְּכַלֶּה״ נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the fourth item of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The listing of בל תכלה as a separate fourth reason.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All the reasons explain leaving the end of the field, which is the content of בל תכלה, so the fourth reason seems redundant.

steps.title: רבא: the fourth reason is about cheaters
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the fourth reason means: to stop cheaters who would falsely claim they already left פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Because of the cheaters.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by giving the fourth reason a specific meaning: preventing cheating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If פאה could be left anywhere, a dishonest owner could harvest everything and claim he left פאה in the middle and the poor already took it. Requiring it at the end makes cheating impossible to hide. So this reason is different from the others: it protects the מצוה itself from dishonest owners.
steps.whatToRemember: There are four reasons for leaving פאה at the field's end: theft from the poor, wasting their time, חשד, and cheaters. The חשד reason proves חז"ל take suspicion seriously, which supports the נר חנוכה rules.

phrases.english: Rava said: Because of the cheaters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the fourth reason is given a distinct, specific meaning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בל תכלה is a general reason that covers all the others.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fourth reason specifically targets cheaters who would falsely claim they already gave פאה.

steps.title: A lamp with two spouts counts for two people
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that one lamp with two wick-spouts can fulfill נר חנוכה for two people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר רדיפה said in the name of רב הונא: A lamp that has two spouts counts for two people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the laws of נר חנוכה with a new ruling about a lamp with two wick openings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each spout holds its own wick, so each flame is clearly separate. That is why the two flames can count as two separate נרות, one for each person.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר רְדִיפָה אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Redifa said in the name of Rav Huna:
A lamp that has two spouts —
counts for two people.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר רְדִיפָה אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, returning to the laws of נר חנוכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lamp with two spouts fulfills נר חנוכה for two people.

steps.title: A bowl ringed with wicks, covered, counts for several people
steps.stepSummary: רבא: a bowl of oil with wicks around it counts for many people if a vessel is turned over on top of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If he filled a bowl with oil and surrounded it with wicks, and turned a vessel upside down over it, it counts for several people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא expands רב הונא's ruling to a bowl with many wicks and adds a condition: it must be covered by an overturned vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering the bowl separates the flames so that each wick looks like its own light. Then each wick can count as a נר for a different person.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If one filled a bowl with oil and surrounded it with wicks:
if he turned a vessel over on top of it —
it counts for several people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רב הונא's principle to a multi-wick bowl.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A covered bowl with several wicks fulfills נר חנוכה for several people.

steps.title: Uncovered, it is a bonfire and counts for no one
steps.stepSummary: Without the covering vessel, the flames merge into a bonfire, which does not count even for one person.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not turn a vessel over it, he made it like a bonfire, and it does not count even for one person.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the other side of his ruling: what happens if the bowl is left uncovered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The flames join into one big blaze, which looks like a bonfire and not a lamp. A מדורה is not a נר at all, so it fails completely, even for a single person.
steps.confusionAlert: It is easy to think an uncovered bowl would at least count for one person. It does not. A bonfire is not a valid נר at all.

phrases.english: If he did not turn a vessel over it —
he has made it like a kind of bonfire,
and it does not count even for one person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite case of step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An uncovered bowl with many wicks is a bonfire and is invalid even for one person.

steps.title: The שבת house lamp beats both נר חנוכה and קידוש
steps.stepSummary: רבא says it is obvious that נר ביתו comes before נר חנוכה and before קידוש היום, because of שלום בית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is obvious to me: between a house lamp and a נר חנוכה, the house lamp comes first because of שלום בית. Between a house lamp and קידוש היום, the house lamp comes first because of שלום בית.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא sets up an order of priority for a poor person who can afford only one מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the שבת lamp the family sits in the dark, which leads to tension and unhappiness. שלום בית outweighs both נר חנוכה and קידוש. רבא says this is פשיטא, simple and clear.

keyTerms.meaning: קידוש, sanctifying the day over wine

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the הלכה that נר שבת comes before נר חנוכה and before wine for קידוש when money is short.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is obvious to me,
between a house lamp and a Chanukah lamp —

phrases.aramaic: נֵר בֵּיתוֹ עָדִיף, מִשּׁוּם שְׁלוֹם בֵּיתוֹ.
phrases.english: the house lamp takes precedence, because of peace in his home.
Between a house lamp and Kiddush of the day —

phrases.aramaic: נֵר בֵּיתוֹ עָדִיף, מִשּׁוּם שְׁלוֹם בֵּיתוֹ.
phrases.english: the house lamp takes precedence, because of peace in his home.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: priorities among מצוות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נר ביתו takes precedence over both נר חנוכה and קידוש היום, because of שלום בית.

steps.title: רבא's question: נר חנוכה or קידוש first?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks which comes first: קידוש, because it is frequent, or נר חנוכה, because it publicizes the miracle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: Between a נר חנוכה and קידוש היום, what is the law? Does קידוש come first because it is frequent, or does נר חנוכה come first because of פרסומי ניסא?
steps.whatsHappening: Having settled the obvious cases, רבא raises a real question about the two remaining מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two competing principles. תדיר ושאינו תדיר, תדיר קודם: a frequent מצוה (קידוש, every week) comes before a rare one. On the other side, נר חנוכה has the special value of publicizing the miracle.

phrases.english: Rava asked:
A Chanukah lamp versus Kiddush of the day, what is the law?
Does Kiddush take precedence, because it is frequent,
or perhaps the Chanukah lamp takes precedence,
because of publicizing the miracle?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the obvious cases to the doubtful one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which takes precedence when only one is affordable: נר חנוכה or קידוש היום.

steps.title: רבא answers his own question: נר חנוכה wins
steps.stepSummary: רבא resolves his question: נר חנוכה comes first because of פרסומי ניסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he asked it, he went back and resolved it: נר חנוכה comes first, because of פרסומי ניסא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own question in favor of נר חנוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Publicizing the miracle outweighs the usual rule that a frequent מצוה comes first. פרסומי ניסא is the central purpose of נר חנוכה, and it carries great weight.
steps.whatToRemember: The order of priority is: נר ביתו, then נר חנוכה, then קידוש היום.

phrases.english: After he asked it, he then resolved it:

phrases.aramaic: נֵר חֲנוּכָּה עֲדִיף, מִשּׁוּם פַּרְסוֹמֵי נִיסָּא.
phrases.english: The Chanukah lamp takes precedence, because of publicizing the miracle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נר חנוכה takes precedence over קידוש היום because of פרסומי ניסא.

steps.title: רב הונא: rewards for being careful with מצוות
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא lists rewards that match each מצוה: lights bring scholarly sons, מזוזה a nice home, ציצית a nice garment, and קידוש plenty of wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: One who regularly lights candles will have sons who are תלמידי חכמים. One careful with מזוזה earns a beautiful home. One careful with ציצית earns a beautiful garment. One careful with קידוש היום earns barrels full of wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to אגדה, listing the rewards for being careful with certain מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each reward matches its מצוה. Light brings sons who spread the light of Torah. מזוזה goes on a house, ציצית on a garment, and קידוש uses wine. The lights mentioned are שבת and חנוכה candles.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is accustomed, does it regularly

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
One who is accustomed to lighting candles
will have sons who are Torah scholars.
One who is careful with mezuzah merits a beautiful home.
One who is careful with tzitzis merits a beautiful garment.
One who is careful with Kiddush of the day
merits to fill barrels of wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the הלכה of lights to the reward for lights and related מצוות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Being careful with lights earns sons who are תלמידי חכמים. Other מצוות earn matching rewards.

steps.title: Story: רב הונא and רבי אבין the carpenter
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא saw that רבי אבין lit many candles and predicted two great sons. רב אידי בר אבין and רב חייא בר אבין came from that home.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא used to pass by the door of רבי אבין the carpenter. He saw that he regularly lit many lights and said, 'Two great men will come from here.' And רב אידי בר אבין and רב חייא בר אבין came from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing רב הונא's statement coming true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבין's many שבת lights showed he was careful with the מצוה. Two great חכמים came from his home, just as רב הונא had said.

phrases.english: Rav Huna was accustomed
to pass by and study
at the doorway of Rabbi Avin the carpenter.
He saw that he regularly lit many lamps,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: תְּרֵי גַּבְרֵי רַבְרְבֵי נָפְקִי מֵהָכָא.
phrases.english: he said: Two great men will come out of here.
There came out of them

phrases.aramaic: רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין וְרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין.
phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin and Rav Chiya bar Avin.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא הֲוָה רְגִיל דַּהֲוָה חָלֵיף וְתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Story illustrating רב הונא's statement.
steps.raayaObject: Lighting many candles brings sons who are תלמידי חכמים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The sons of רבי אבין the carpenter.

steps.title: Story: רב חסדא and the family of רב שיזבי
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא saw a family lighting many candles and predicted a great man. רב שיזבי came from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא used to pass by the door of רב שיזבי's family home. He saw they regularly lit many lights and said, 'A great man will come from here.' And רב שיזבי came from them.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story backs up the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, a home careful with many lights produced a great תלמיד חכם. A second example strengthens רב הונא's statement.
steps.whatToRemember: Care with שבת and חנוכה lights is linked to having sons who are תלמידי חכמים, as two stories from רב הונא and רב חסדא show.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda was accustomed
to pass by and study
at the doorway of the family home of Rav Sheizvi.
phrases.notes: That is, the home of רב שיזבי's father's family, before רב שיזבי was born or grown.

phrases.english: He saw that they regularly lit many lamps,
he said: A great man will come out of here.
Rav Sheizvi came out of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא הֲוָה רְגִיל דַּהֲוָה חָלֵיף וְתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel second story supporting the same point.
steps.raayaObject: Lighting many candles brings sons who are תלמידי חכמים.

steps.title: רב יוסף tells his wife not to light late
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף's wife lit the שבת candles late. He brings a ברייתא about the pillars of cloud and fire overlapping to show that one should light a little early.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף's wife used to light the candles late. רב יוסף said to her: We learned that the verse 'The pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night did not depart' teaches that the pillar of cloud overlapped with the pillar of fire, and the pillar of fire overlapped with the pillar of cloud.
steps.whatsHappening: A story: רב יוסף corrects his wife for lighting late and supports himself with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each pillar appeared before the other one left, so there was an overlap. In the same way, שבת should be brought in a little before dark, so one should light early and not at the last minute.

phrases.english: The wife of Rav Yosef
would light late.
Rav Yosef said to her:
We learned in a baraita
"The pillar of cloud by day did not depart,
nor the pillar of fire by night"

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁעַמּוּד עָנָן מַשְׁלִים לְעַמּוּד הָאֵשׁ
phrases.english: this teaches that the pillar of cloud overlapped with the pillar of fire,
phrases.notes: The fire appeared before the cloud left at evening.

phrases.english: and the pillar of fire overlapped with the pillar of cloud.
phrases.notes: So too, one should light a bit before night.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵיתְהוּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף הֲוָת מְאַחֲרָה וּמַדְלְקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of שבת candles from the stories about lighting many candles.
steps.raayaObject: One should light שבת candles a little before nightfall, not late.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on שמות 13:22 about the overlapping pillars.

steps.title: An elder: not too early and not too late
steps.stepSummary: After the correction, the wife thought she should light very early. An elder quotes a ברייתא that one should light neither too early nor too late.
steps.simpleTranslation: She then thought she should light very early. A certain elder said to her: We learned, 'As long as one does not light too early and does not light too late.'
steps.whatsHappening: The wife goes too far the other way, and an elder gives the balanced rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's proof only showed that one should not be late. Lighting much too early is also wrong, because then the lighting does not look like it is in honor of שבת. The rule is to light close to the start of שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: Light שבת candles at the right time: not too early and not too late.

phrases.english: She then thought to light very early.
A certain elder said to her:
We learned:
as long as he does not light too early and does not light too late.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְבַרָה לְאַקְדּוֹמֵי. אֲמַר לַהּ הָהוּא סָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits how far one should take רב יוסף's teaching.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The right time to light is near the start of שבת, neither much earlier nor late.

steps.title: רבא: rewards for loving, honoring, and fearing Torah scholars
steps.stepSummary: רבא lists rewards that match how a person treats תלמידי חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: One who loves Torah scholars will have sons who are Torah scholars. One who honors Torah scholars will have sons-in-law who are Torah scholars. One who fears Torah scholars will himself become a Torah scholar. And if he is not capable of that, his words will be listened to like those of a Torah scholar.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a teaching about rewards, in the same style as רב הונא's list of rewards for מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each reward matches the attitude. Love brings scholarly children, honor brings scholarly sons-in-law, and awe brings Torah to the person himself. Even someone without the ability will have his words respected like a scholar's.

phrases.english: Rava said:
One who loves Torah scholars
will have sons who are Torah scholars.
One who honors Torah scholars
will have sons-in-law who are Torah scholars.
One who stands in awe of Torah scholars
will himself become a Torah scholar.
And if he is not capable of this,
his words will be heard like those of a Torah scholar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: דְּרָחֵים רַבָּנַן, הָווּ לֵיהּ בְּנִין רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another reward list, like רב הונא's list in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: How a person treats Torah scholars determines whether Torah comes to his children, his sons-in-law, or himself.

steps.title: What is burnt oil?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's phrase 'not with שמן שריפה' and asks what that oil is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And not with burnt oil, etc.' What is burnt oil?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and asks for the meaning of a term. This sets up רבה's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name 'burnt oil' is unclear, since oil that has already burned cannot be used. The גמרא first needs to define it before it can discuss why it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: 'burning oil', oil that is meant to be burned

phrases.english: The mishna said: "And not with burnt oil, etc."
What is burnt oil?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא בְּשֶׁמֶן שְׂרֵיפָה וְכוּ׳: מַאי שֶׁמֶן שְׂרֵיפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה and returns to the משנה.

steps.title: רבה: impure תרומה oil, meant to be burned
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that it is תרומה oil that became טמא. It is called 'burnt oil' because it must be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: It is oil of תרומה that became impure. And why do they call it 'burnt oil'? Because it is meant to be burned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defines the term and explains where the name comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impure תרומה may not be eaten, so the only thing to do with it is burn it. Since it is destined for burning, it is named after its end.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
Oil of terumah that became impure.
And why do they call it "burnt oil"?
Because it is destined to be burned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: שֶׁמֶן שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה שֶׁנִּטְמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמן שריפה is impure תרומה oil, called this because it must be burned.

steps.title: Why is it forbidden on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why this oil may not be used for שבת candles.
steps.simpleTranslation: And on שבת, what is the reason one may not light with it?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the oil is defined, the גמרא asks for the reason it is forbidden. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning this oil is exactly what one is supposed to do with it, so it seems like a good use for שבת lights. The גמרא wants to know what the problem is.

phrases.english: And on Shabbat, what is the reason one may not light with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the definition by asking for the reason of the prohibition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why using impure תרומה oil for שבת lights is forbidden.

steps.title: A decree in case he tilts the lamp
steps.stepSummary: Since there is a מצוה to burn this oil, one might tilt the lamp on שבת to make it burn faster, so חז"ל forbade it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since there is a מצוה on him to burn it, it is a decree in case he tilts the lamp.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא, continuing רבה's view, gives the reason: a rabbinic decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person wants this oil used up, because burning it is a מצוה. He might tilt the lamp to bring the oil to the wick, which is a forbidden act of kindling on שבת. To prevent that, חז"ל forbade lighting with it.

keyTerms.meaning: to burn it, to get rid of it
a rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
in case he tilts the lamp

phrases.english: Since it is a מצוה for him to burn it,
it is a decree in case he tilts the lamp.
phrases.notes: Tilting brings the oil closer to the wick, which counts as kindling.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁמִּצְוָה עָלָיו לְבַעֲרוֹ, גְּזֵרָה שֶׁמָּא יַטֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שמא יטה: because he is eager to burn it, he may tilt the lamp.

steps.title: אביי: then it should be allowed on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that if the only worry is tilting, the oil should be allowed on יום טוב, where tilting is permitted. Yet a משנה forbids it on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But if so, it should be permitted on יום טוב! Why then did we learn: 'One may not light with burnt oil on יום טוב'?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבה's reason by pointing to the יום טוב case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב, kindling and adjusting a flame are permitted, so 'in case he tilts' should not be a concern. If the oil is still forbidden on יום טוב, the tilting reason does not seem to explain the law.

keyTerms.meaning: but if so, according to your view

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But if so, it should be permitted on a Festival!
Why then did we learn:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַדְלִיקִין בְּשֶׁמֶן שְׂרֵיפָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב? —
phrases.english: "One may not light with burnt oil on a Festival"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in step 21.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The tilting worry does not apply on יום טוב, yet the משנה still forbids the oil on יום טוב.

steps.title: יום טוב is forbidden because of שבת
steps.stepSummary: The answer: חז"ל forbade it on יום טוב too, so that people would not come to use it on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree on יום טוב because of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה: the יום טוב rule is an extra decree tied to שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tilting worry is truly only about שבת. If people were allowed this oil on יום טוב, they might use it on שבת as well. So חז"ל forbade it on both days.
steps.confusionAlert: The יום טוב prohibition does not come from tilting on יום טוב itself. It is a safeguard so that people will not mix up יום טוב and שבת.

phrases.english: It is a decree on a Festival because of Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extending a decree (a גזירה protecting another rule)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the tilting concern on יום טוב, the oil should be permitted then.
steps.terutzMaskana: The oil is forbidden on יום טוב as a safeguard for שבת.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the case is יום טוב on Friday
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rejects the tilting concern. He says the משנה is about יום טוב that falls on ערב שבת, when the candles are lit on יום טוב, and קדשים may not be burned on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: We are not worried that he may tilt the lamp. Rather, here we are dealing with יום טוב that falls on ערב שבת, because one may not burn holy items on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא offers a completely different explanation of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When יום טוב falls on Friday, the שבת candles are lit while it is still יום טוב. Impure תרומה counts as holy, and holy items may not be burned on יום טוב. So the problem is burning קדשים on יום טוב, not tilting the lamp.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
We are not concerned that he may tilt the lamp.
Rather, here, with a Festival
that fell on Shabbat eve, we are dealing,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין שׂוֹרְפִין קׇדָשִׁים בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: because one may not burn holy items on a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: לְשֶׁמָּא יַטֶּה לָא חָיְישִׁינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבה's reason and moves the case to יום טוב on ערב שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Impure תרומה oil is forbidden because burning קדשים is not allowed on יום טוב, and the משנה is about יום טוב falling on Friday.

steps.title: But the משנה lists יום טוב separately
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא: a later clause of the משנה forbids this oil on יום טוב, which implies that the first clause is not about יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the later clause teaches 'One may not light with burnt oil on יום טוב,' we can infer that the first clause is not dealing with יום טוב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חסדא's reading using the structure of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first clause were already about יום טוב, there would be no need for a separate clause about יום טוב. Since there is a separate clause, the first clause seems to be about a regular שבת.

phrases.english: But since the later clause teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַדְלִיקִין בְּשֶׁמֶן שְׂרֵיפָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: "One may not light with burnt oil on a Festival,"

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּרֵישָׁא לָאו בְּיוֹם טוֹב עָסְקִינַן!
phrases.english: we can infer that the first clause is not dealing with a Festival!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's reading of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the first clause is about יום טוב on ערב שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A separate יום טוב clause implies that the first clause is about an ordinary שבת.

steps.title: רב חנינא מסורא: the later clause gives the reason
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא מסורא answers that the later clause is not a new law. It explains the reason for the first clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא from סורא said: The משנה is saying 'what is the reason.' What is the reason one may not light with burnt oil on יום טוב that falls on ערב שבת? Because one may not burn holy items on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנינא defends רב חסדא by reading the later clause as an explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later clause does not start a separate case. It tells us why the first clause forbids the oil: on יום טוב, holy items may not be burned. So both clauses are about יום טוב, and רב חסדא's reading holds.
steps.whatToRemember: Two views on שמן שריפה. רבה: forbidden on שבת because one may tilt the lamp, and on יום טוב as a safeguard for שבת. רב חסדא: the case is יום טוב on ערב שבת, and burning קדשים on יום טוב is forbidden. Per רב חנינא מסורא, the later clause explains this reason.

phrases.english: Rav Chanina from Sura said:
The mishna is saying "what is the reason":

phrases.aramaic: מַה טַּעַם אֵין מַדְלִיקִין בְּשֶׁמֶן שְׂרֵיפָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב —
phrases.english: What is the reason one may not light with burnt oil on a Festival (that falls on Shabbat eve)?

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין שׂוֹרְפִין קׇדָשִׁים בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: Because one may not burn holy items on a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חֲנִינָא מִסּוּרָא: מַה טַּעַם קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The later clause is a separate law, so the first clause must be about an ordinary שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The later clause explains the first clause, so both are about יום טוב.
